In the week ending October 31, the advance figure for seasonally adjusted initial claims was 189,000, a decrease of
6,000 from the previous week's revised level. The previous week's level was revised up by 1,000 from 194,000 to
195,000. The 4-week moving average was 194,750, a decrease of 2,250 from the previous week's revised average. The
previous week's average was revised up by 250 from 196,750 to 197,000.
The advance seasonally adjusted insured unemployment rate was 1.1 percent for the week ending October 24,
unchanged from the previous week's unrevised rate. The advance number for seasonally adjusted insured
unemployment during the week ending October 24 was 1,718,000, an increase of 23,000 from the previous week's
revised level. The previous week's level was revised down by 6,000 from 1,701,000 to 1,695,000. The 4-week moving
average was 1,709,500, an increase of 1,000 from the previous week's revised average. The previous week's average was
revised down by 1,500 from 1,710,000 to 1,708,500.

2

UNADJUSTED DATA
The advance number of actual initial claims under state programs, unadjusted, totaled 176,698 in the week ending
October 31, a decrease of 2,951 (or -1.6 percent) from the previous week. The seasonal factors had expected an increase
of 2,539 (or 1.4 percent) from the previous week. There were 216,026 initial claims in the comparable week in 2025.
The advance unadjusted insured unemployment rate was 1.0 percent during the week ending October 24, unchanged
from the prior week. The advance unadjusted level of insured unemployment in state programs totaled 1,494,812, an
increase of 10,189 (or 0.7 percent) from the preceding week. The seasonal factors had expected a decrease of 10,169
(or -0.7 percent) from the previous week. A year earlier the rate was 1.1 percent and the volume was 1,712,402.

The total number of continued weeks claimed for benefits in all programs for the week ending October 17 was
1,507,702, an increase of 8,510 from the previous week. There were 1,756,507 weekly claims filed for benefits in all
programs in the comparable week in 2025.
No state was triggered "on" the Extended Benefits program during the week ending October 17.
Initial claims for UI benefits filed by former Federal civilian employees totaled 552 in the week ending October 24, an
increase of 110 from the prior week. There were 347 initial claims filed by newly discharged veterans, a decrease of 40
from the preceding week.
There were 5,128 continued weeks claimed filed by former Federal civilian employees the week ending October 17, an
increase of 194 from the previous week. Newly discharged veterans claiming benefits totaled 4,941, a decrease of 34
from the prior week.

3

The highest insured unemployment rates in the week ending October 17 were in New Jersey (2.0), Washington (1.8),
California (1.7), Massachusetts (1.7), Puerto Rico (1.6), Nevada (1.5), Oregon (1.5), Rhode Island (1.5), New York (1.4),
and Illinois (1.3).
The largest increases in initial claims for the week ending October 24 were in New York (+2,609), Texas (+1,564),
California (+1,043), Pennsylvania (+818), and Ohio (+784), while the largest decreases were in Michigan (-1,813),
Tennessee (-977), South Carolina (-763), Kentucky (-496), and Oklahoma (-227).

Note: Advance claims are not directly comparable to claims reported in prior weeks. Advance claims are reported by the
state liable for paying the unemployment compensation, whereas previous weeks reported claims reflect claimants by
state of residence. In addition, claims reported as "workshare equivalent" in the previous week are added to the advance
claims as a proxy for the current week's "workshare equivalent" activity.
